goal: Promote the adaptive cache engine from repo-only research code into the ordinary GAYA-CENTRAL command surface while preserving reconstructibility, rollback, and benchmarkability.
north_star: Increase capability and performance together; keep generated runtime state disposable.

runtime_model.projection: selective hot-pyc wheel for the active CPython cache tag
runtime_model.control_plane: control.whl remains latest known-good across app rollback
runtime_model.activation: candidate smoke -> manifest -> atomic symlink switch
runtime_model.verification: full SHA on identity change; local artifact-epoch identity reuse when unchanged

safety_invariants: candidate is smoke-tested before first activation
normal commands use current app plane
runtime-* commands use latest known-good control plane
source Python remains in projected wheel as fallback
native accelerator and hot-pyc wheel are rebuildable caches
prune must preserve current, previous, control and their canonical source wheels

benchmark_contract.cache_benchmark: scalar reference vs adaptive engine with parity gate
benchmark_contract.runtime_benchmark: same-artifact reactivation plus installed process startup/command latency

stop_reason: Same immutable artifact reactivation is sub-millisecond, pointer switching is about one tenth of a millisecond, selective hot-pyc dominates broader bytecode projection, compression changes were negligible, and fast-dispatch improvements had fallen to low-single-digit milliseconds.
